verses.zh: （困苦人发昏的时候，在耶和华面前吐露苦情的祷告。）耶和华啊，求你听我的祷告，容我的呼求达到你面前！
verses.en: The prayer of an oppressed man, as he grows faint and pours out his lament before the Lord.O Lord, hear my prayer.Pay attention to my cry for help.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 102. The psalmist laments his oppressed state, but longs for a day when the Lord will restore Jerusalem and vindicate his suffering people.
verses.commentary:
102:1-7 This strophe describes the psalmist's situation (i.e., "the day of my distress,"
Ps. 102:2,23-26; see Psalm 6).

- feels YHWH has hidden His face (i.e., no sense of His presence)

- his days are consumed in smoke, Ps. 102:3

- his bones have been scorched, Ps. 102:3

- his heart has been smitten, Ps. 102:4

- he has forgotten to eat because of his loud groaning, Ps. 102:4b-5a

- his bones cling to his flesh, Ps. 103:5b

- he looks like a bird of the wilderness, Ps. 102:6,7b

- he cannot sleep, Ps. 102:7a

It is possible that what looks like physical illness is really a person
grieving over exile and the loss of the temple (cf. Ps. 102:14,18-22,23-28).

102:1-2 The Psalm opens with a series of prayer requests.

- hear my prayer ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE,
cf. Ps. 17:6; 39:12; 54:2; 55:1; 61:1; 64:1; 143:1

- let my cry for help come to You ‒ BDB 9, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- do not hide Your face from me ‒ BDB 711, KB 771, Hiphil JUSSIVE,
cf. Ps. 27:9; 69:17; 143:7

- incline Your ear to me ‒ BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil IMPERATIVE,
cf. Ps. 17:6; 31:2; 71:2; 86:1; 88:2

- quickly ‒ BDB 554, KB 553, Piel IMPERATIVE (lit. "be quick,"
see NJB, most English translations translate it as an ADVERB [BDB 555])

- answer me ‒ BDB 772, KB 851, Qal IMPERATIVE

102:1 "Lord" This is the covenant name for Israel's God
(cf. vv. 1, 12, 15, 18, 21, 22). It is first used (not in Genesis 1, which has Elohim) in
Gen. 2:4 (i.e., the special creation of Adam and Eve).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

verses.zh: 我在急难的日子，求你向我侧耳；不要向我掩面！我呼求的日子，求你快快应允我！
verses.en: Do not ignore me in my time of trouble.[NOTE:1] Listen to me.[NOTE:2] When I call out to you, quickly answer me.
notes: Heb “and may my cry for help come to you.”

Heb “do not hide your face from me in the day of my trouble.” The idiom “to hide the face” can mean “to ignore” (see Pss 10:11; 13:1; 51:9) or carry the stronger idea of “to reject” (see Pss 29:7; 30:7; 88:14).
verses.commentary:
102:2 "Your face" This is a Hebrew
idiom for the personal presence of YHWH (cf. Num. 6:25; Ps. 10:11; 13:1; 27:9; 30:7; 44:24;
51:9; 69:17; 80:3,7,19; 88:14; 143:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "day" This imagery (BDB 398) is repeated five times.

- in the day of my distress, Ps. 102:2a

- in the day when I call, Ps. 102:2c

- my days, Ps. 102:3a

- all day long, Ps. 102:8a

- my days, Ps. 102:11

The Hebrew word yom can be literal or figurative.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DAY (yom)

▣ "Your ear" This is anthropomorphic imagery. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism).

verses.zh: 因为，我的年日如烟云消灭；我的骨头如火把烧着。
verses.en: For my days go up in smoke,[NOTE:1] and my bones are charred as in a fireplace.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “turn toward me your ear.”
Heb “for my days come to an end in smoke.”
verses.commentary:
102:3 This verse used fire imagery to describe the psalmist's current situation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

verses.zh: 我的心被伤，如草枯干，甚至我忘记吃饭。
verses.en: My heart is parched[NOTE:1] and withered like grass,for I am unable[NOTE:2] to eat food.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew noun קֵד (qed, “fireplace”) occurs only here, in Isa 33:14 (where it refers to the fire itself), and perhaps in Lev 6:2.
Heb “struck, attacked.”
Heb “I forget.”

verses.zh: 因我唉哼的声音，我的肉紧贴骨头。
verses.en: Because of the anxiety that makes me groan,my bones protrude from my skin.[NOTE:1]
notes: I am unable to eat food. During his time of mourning, the psalmist refrained from eating. In the following verse he describes metaphorically the physical effects of fasting.

verses.zh: 我如同旷野的鹈鹕；我好像荒场的鴞鸟。
verses.en: I am like an owl[NOTE:1] in the wilderness;I am like a screech owl[NOTE:2] among the ruins.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “from the sound of my groaning my bone[s] stick to my flesh.” The preposition at the beginning of the verse is causal; the phrase “sound of my groaning” is metonymic for the anxiety that causes the groaning. The point seems to be this: Anxiety (which causes the psalmist to groan) keeps him from eating (v. 4). This physical deprivation in turn makes him emaciated—he is turned to “skin and bones,” so to speak.

The Hebrew term קָאַת (qaʾat) refers to some type of bird (see Lev 11:18; Deut 14:17) that was typically found near ruins (see Zeph 2:14). Modern translations have frequently rendered this as some type of owl (NIV, REB “desert owl”; NRSV “owl”).
The Hebrew term כוֹס (khos) refers to a bird (see Lev 11:17; Deut 14:16), probably a type of owl (cf. NIV, REB “owl”; NRSV “little owl”).
verses.commentary:
102:6 "pelican. . .owl" Often in the
OT, birds and wild animals are used to denote not only abandoned places, but the
presence of the demonic (i.e., Isa. 13:19-22; 34:11-15; Zeph. 2:14). Here the
focus is on the element of abandonment or aloneness.

Also note the birds mentioned are Levitically unclean (cf. Lev.
11:13-19), which is another way to assert the sense of rejection! See UBS, Fauna
and Flora of the Bible.

verses.zh: 我警醒不睡；我像房顶上孤单的麻雀。
verses.en: I stay awake;[NOTE:1] I am like a solitary bird on a roof.
notes: By comparing himself to a screech owl among the ruins, the psalmist may be highlighting his loneliness (see v. 7), though he may also be comparing his cries for help to the owl’s screech.

verses.zh: 我的仇敌终日辱骂我；向我猖狂的人指着我赌咒。
verses.en: All day long my enemies taunt me;those who mock me use my name in their curses.[NOTE:1]
notes: This probably refers to the psalmist’s inability to sleep. Another option is to translate, “I keep watch,” in which case it might refer to watching for a response from the Lord (see vv. 1-2).
verses.commentary:
102:8-11 This strophe continues the
description of the hurting psalmist.

- his enemies (possibly invaders) reproach him continuously, Ps. 102:8

- his enemies deride him

- his enemies use his name as a curse (cf. Isa. 65:15; Jer. 29:22)

- he has eaten ashes and drunk tears (these were signs of mourning, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES, cf. Ps. 42:3; 80:5)

- same as #4

- his days are like a lengthened shadow (i.e., his pain lasts a long time)

- he withers away like grass (cf. Gen. 6:3; Job 10:4; 14:1-2; Ps. 78:39; 90:5-6;
102:4; 103:15-18; Isa. 40:6; 1 Pet. 1:24-25)

The theological issue is why was he suffering. Psalm 102:10
reveals that he was experiencing divine judgment (cf. Psalm 38). One wonders if
he is a symbol or representative of the nation (cf. Ps. 102:12-17,18-22).

102:8b

The MT has "those who deride me" (BDB 237 II, KB 248, Poal
PARTICIPLE. The basic root הלל has two distinct and

- praise, KB 248 II

The UBS Text Project, p. 375, cannot decide which one is
original. Number 1 implies the psalmist's enemies were close friends or covenant
partners. Number 2 implies the enemies were foreign nations who
exiled God's people.

verses.zh: 我吃过炉灰，如同吃饭；我所喝的与眼泪搀杂。
verses.en: For I eat ashes as if they were bread,[NOTE:1] and mix my drink with my tears,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “by me they swear.” When the psalmist’s enemies call judgment down on others, they hold the psalmist up as a prime example of what they desire their enemies to become.
Mourners would sometimes put ashes on their head or roll in ashes as a sign of mourning (see 2 Sam 13:19; Job 2:8; Isa 58:5).

verses.zh: 这都因你的恼恨和忿怒；你把我拾起来，又把我摔下去。
verses.en: because of your anger and raging fury.Indeed,[NOTE:1] you pick me up and throw me away.
notes: Heb “weeping.”

verses.zh: 我的年日如日影偏斜；我也如草枯干。
verses.en: My days are coming to an end,[NOTE:1] and I am withered like grass.
notes: Or “for.”

verses.zh: 惟你―耶和华必存到永远；你可记念的名也存到万代。
verses.en: But you, O Lord, rule forever,[NOTE:1] and your reputation endures.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my days [are] like an extended [or “lengthening”] shadow,” that is, like a late afternoon shadow made by the descending sun that will soon be swallowed up by complete darkness.
Heb “sit” (i.e., sit enthroned, see Ps 9:7). The imperfect verbal form highlights the generalization.
verses.commentary:
102:12-17 This strophe has a national emphasis. YHWH has an international purpose for Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

Notice the things the psalmist asserts about YHWH.

- He sits enthroned forever (cf. Ps. 9:7; 10:16; 29:10; Lam. 5:19)

- His name (lit. "remembrance," BDB 271, cf. Ps. 30:4; 97:12) abides to all generations
(cf. Exod. 3:15; Ps. 135:13; also note Ps. 100:5; 119:90)

- He acts in grace toward His covenant people

- He has built up Zion

- He has appeared (i.e., to Zion) in His glory

- He regards the prayers of the destitute (BDB 792, occurs only here and Jer. 17:6,
where it is used of a tree/scrub; the root comes from the VERB, "to strip bare")

The psalmist asks YHWH to act on Israel's behalf for His greater purpose!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

verses.zh: 你必起来怜恤锡安，因现在是可怜她的时候，日期已经到了。
verses.en: You will rise up and have compassion on Zion.[NOTE:1] For it is time to have mercy on her,for the appointed time has come.
notes: Heb “and your remembrance [is] for a generation and a generation.”
verses.commentary:
102:13 "You will arise" This VERB (BDB 877, KB 1086) has a
wide semantic field. It could denote

- YHWH rising from His throne to act (cf. Ps. 119:126)

- YHWH awaking from sleep (imagery for His lack of action)

- YHWH becoming active after a period of purposeful inactivity

▣ "Zion" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

▣ "the appointed time has come" The NOUN (BDB 417) has
the connotation of "an appointed time" (cf. Ps. 75:2; Dan. 8:19). The concept that YHWH is in control
of time, space, history is central to the character of the one true creator God (cf. Ecclesiastes 3).

verses.zh: 你的仆人原来喜悦她的石头，可怜她的尘土。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] your servants take delight in her stonesand feel compassion for[NOTE:2] the dust of her ruins.[NOTE:3]
notes: The imperfect verbal forms are understood as expressing the psalmist’s confidence in God’s intervention. Another option is to take them as expressing the psalmist’s request or wish, “You, rise up and have compassion!”
Or “for.”
The Poel of חָנַן (khanan) occurs only here and in Prov 14:21, where it refers to having compassion on the poor.
verses.commentary:
102:14-17 These verses imply the destruction of the temple.

- the nations (i.e., who did this) will fear, Ps. 102:15

- YHWH will build up Zion and show her His glory, Ps. 102:16

- the prayers of the destitute (i.e., the exiled people of God) will be heard

- note Ps. 102:18-22

102:14 "Surely Your servants find pleasure in her stones" This phrase reminds
me of the deep emotional attachment that modern Judaism has for the wailing wall in
Jerusalem (i.e., the foundation stones of Solomon's temple). Judaism (i.e., the Mosaic Law)
is linked to a special place of worship (i.e., the tabernacle, later the temple in Jerusalem).

▣ "her dust" This NOUN (BDB 779, KB 862) is often used of the debris of
destroyed cities (cf. 1 Kgs. 20:10; Neh. 4:2,10; Ezek. 26:4,12).

verses.zh: 列国要敬畏耶和华的名；世上诸王都敬畏你的荣耀。
verses.en: The nations will respect the reputation of the Lord,[NOTE:1] and all the kings of the earth will respect[NOTE:2] his splendor
notes: Heb “her dust,” probably referring to the dust of the city’s rubble.
Heb “will fear the name of the Lord.” To “fear” God’s name means to have a healthy respect for his revealed reputation which in turn motivates one to obey God’s commands (see Ps 86:11).
verses.commentary:
102:15 "the nations will fear" Through the years of my Bible study, I have become convinced
that YHWH has always desired the salvation and restoration of all humans made in His image. I have
tried to document this basic presupposition in the following Special Topic.

Of course, this brings up the question about God's OT promises to the nation of Israel.
I have also tried to document the revelatory change from the OT to the NT in a Special Topic (see below).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE OT COVENANT PROMISES SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR

verses.zh: 因为耶和华建造了锡安，在他荣耀里显现。
verses.en: when the Lord rebuilds Zionand reveals his splendor,

verses.zh: 他垂听穷人的祷告，并不藐视他们的祈求。
verses.en: when he responds to the prayer of the destitute[NOTE:1] and does not reject[NOTE:2] their request.[NOTE:3]
notes: The verb “will fear” is understood by ellipsis in the second line (see the preceding line).
The Hebrew adjective עַרְעָר (ʿarar, “destitute”) occurs only here in the OT. It is derived from the verbal root ערר (“to strip oneself”).
Heb “despise.”

verses.zh: 这必为后代的人记下，将来受造的民要赞美耶和华。
verses.en: The account of his intervention[NOTE:1] will be recorded for future generations;people yet to be born[NOTE:2] will praise the Lord.
notes: The perfect verbal forms in vv. 16-17 are functioning as future perfects, indicating future actions that will precede the future developments described in v. 15.
The Hebrew text has simply “this,” referring to the anticipated divine intervention on behalf of Zion (vv. 13, 16-17). The referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
102:18-22 This strophe is a promise
about YHWH's restoration of His covenant people to Judah and her temple.

Hebrews 1 quotes Ps. 102:25-27 as relating to Jesus. In this
sense Ps. 102:28 relates to the new people of God (i.e., believing Jews and
Gentiles, cf. Rom. 2:28-29; 9:6; Gal. 3:7-9,13-14,29; 6:15-16)! In my opinion, Jesus is the
ultimate and final revelation of God, therefore, we must view the OT through the eyes of
the NT and not the other way around. The NT is about Jesus, not Israel.

102:18a Revelation is recorded to document and explain YHWH's will and actions.
They become the basic guidelines for His people in each successive generation. Faithful
followers honor, respect, and obey Scripture (i.e., Ps. 119:105; Prov. 6:23).

verses.zh: 要垂听被囚之人的叹息，要释放将要死的人，
verses.en: in order to hear the painful cries of the prisonersand to set free those condemned to die,[NOTE:1]
notes: The perfect verbal forms in v. 19 are functioning as future perfects, indicating future actions that will precede the future developments described in v. 18.
verses.commentary:
102:20 These images refer to exiled
Judeans (and possibly Israelites).

verses.zh: 使人在锡安传扬耶和华的名，在耶路撒冷传扬赞美他的话，
verses.en: so they may proclaim the name of the Lord in Zionand praise him[NOTE:1] in Jerusalem[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the sons of death.” The phrase “sons of death” (see also Ps 79:11) is idiomatic for those condemned to die.
Heb “his praise.”
verses.commentary: 102:21 This is a prayer that the exiled may return to Judah.

verses.zh: 就是在万民和列国聚会事奉耶和华的时候。
verses.en: when the nations gather together,and the kingdoms pay tribute to the Lord.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
102:22 This, like so many Psalms in
Book IV, has a universal emphasis (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). The phrase, "the kingdom will serve the
Lord," reminds me of Rev. 5:9-14 and 11:15!

verses.zh: 他使我的力量中道衰弱，使我的年日短少。
verses.en: He has taken away my strength in the middle of life;[NOTE:1] he has cut short my days.
notes: “and the kingdoms to serve the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
102:23-28 This strophe, like the two
previous ones, uses personal imagery in a national sense. It affirms YHWH's act
of creation (Ps. 102:26); He is eternal (102:27)! His people have gone through a
devastating time (defeat, destruction, exile), but He will restore them (102:28)
because as "heaven and earth" are the work of His hands (cf. Ps. 8:6; 19:1; Isa.
45:12; 48:13), so too, the covenant people (cf. Ps. 138:8; 143:5; Isa. 45:11;
60:2; 64:8; even Assyria, Isa. 19:25).

102:23-24 The LXX translates these
verses as YHWH speaking to the psalmist. The NT book of Hebrews 1:10-12 quotes
Ps. 102:25-27 as referring to Jesus. The MT translates the same Hebrew
consonants in a different way (cf. Tyndale OT Commentaries, vol. 16,
Psalms 73-150, pp. 395-396).

102:23 "strength" The term (BDB 470)
was used of national strength being affected by YHWH's judgment (cf. Lev. 26:20;
Lam. 1:6,14; Amos 2:14).

▣ "the way" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

verses.zh: 我说：我的　神啊，不要使我中年去世。你的年数世世无穷！
verses.en: I say, “O my God, please do not take me away in the middle of my life.[NOTE:1] You endure through all generations.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he has afflicted my strength in the way.” The term “way” refers here to the course of the psalmist’s life, which appears to be ending prematurely (vv. 23b-24).
Heb “do not lift me up in the middle of my days.”
verses.commentary:
102:24 "O my God" This VOCATIVE uses the general ANE name/title
for deity, El.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A.

verses.zh: 你起初立了地的根基；天也是你手所造的。
verses.en: In earlier times you established the earth;the skies are your handiwork.
verses.commentary:
102:25-27 These verses from the LXX
are quoted in Heb. 1:10-11, where they are applied to Jesus (cf. Heb. 13:8).

verses.zh: 天地都要灭没，你却要长存；天地都要如外衣渐渐旧了。你要将天地如里衣更换，天地就都改变了。
verses.en: They will perish,but you will endure.[NOTE:1] They will wear out like a garment;like clothes you will remove them and they will disappear.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in a generation of generations [are] your years.”
Heb “stand.”

verses.zh: 惟有你永不改变；你的年数没有穷尽。
verses.en: But you remain;[NOTE:1] your years do not come to an end.
notes: The Hebrew verb חָלַף (khalaf) occurs twice in this line, once in the Hiphil (“you will remove them”) and once in the Qal (“they will disappear”). The repetition draws attention to the statement.
verses.commentary:
102:27 "But You are the same" YHWH
does not change nor do His purposes (cf. Ps. 33:11; Mal. 3:6; James 1:17). Psalm

102:27 is a dramatic contrast to 102:26. Even heaven and earth will pass away
(cf. Isa. 34:4; 51:6; Matt. 5:18; 24:35; Mark 13:31; Luke 21:33; 2 Pet. 3:10;
Rev. 20:11), but not YHWH!

For a good brief discussion of God's unchangeableness see
Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 304-308.

verses.zh: 你仆人的子孙要长存；他们的后裔要坚立在你面前。
verses.en: The children of your servants will settle down here,and their descendants[NOTE:1] will live securely in your presence.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you [are] he,” or “you [are] the one.” The statement may echo the Lord’s affirmation “I am he” in Isa 41:4; 43:10, 13; 46:10; 48:12. In each of these passages the affirmation emphasizes the fact that the Lord transcends time limitations, the very point being made in Ps 102:27.
Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”
verses.commentary:
102:28 The VERBS of v. 28 are so encouraging. Faithful
followers will dwell with YHWH forever (cf. Ps. 23:6).

- "will continue" ‒ BDB 1014, KB 1496, Qal IMPERFECT,
basically meaning

- "to settle down," cf. 2 Sam. 7:10; 1 Chr. 17:9

- "to abide in peace and security," cf. Deut. 33:12; Ps. 16:9; Jer. 23:6; 33:16

- this is imagery of a secure homeland guarded by YHWH, cf. 1 Pet. 1:3-5

- "will be established" ‒ BDb 465, KB 464, Niphal IMPERFECT,
basically meaning "firmly established"

- the world, cf. 1 Chr. 16:30; Ps. 93:1; 96:10

- the covenant people, cf. 2 Sam. 7:16; Ps. 89:4

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the
Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- Is this Psalm about an individual or the nation?

- Explain the imagery of Ps. 102:6-7.

- Does Ps. 102:14 imply a reference to the destruction of the temple?

- Does the universal emphasis of Ps. 102:15,22 refer to restoration from exile or an eschatological setting?

- Are heaven and earth permanent or transitory?

- How is Ps. 102:28 related to

- Gen. 12:1-3

- Rom. 2:28-29

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT
PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in
the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one
and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 102:1-7

1Hear my prayer, O Lord!

And let my cry for help come
to You.

2Do not hide Your
face from me in the day of my distress;

Incline Your ear to me;

In the day when I call answer
me quickly.

3For my days have
been consumed in smoke,

And my bones have been
scorched like a hearth.

4My heart has been
smitten like grass and has withered away,

Indeed, I forget to eat my
bread.

5Because of the
loudness of my groaning

My bones cling to my flesh.

6I resemble a
pelican of the wilderness;

I have become like an owl of
the waste places.

7I lie awake,

I have become like a lonely
bird on a housetop.
